ORIGINAL EVIDENCE:
The temperature-dependent dielectric constant ( e '-T ) at different frequencies and at different DC bias electric fields E bias for the series of samples with y = 0.24 and varied x is shown in Fig. 7a-c. A sharp frequency-independent dielectric peak at * 853.1 K under E bias = 0 V, which is corresponding to the longrange ordered FE to paraelectric (PE) phase transition [48], can be observed for the sample y 0.24 x 0.01. Both the samples y 0.24 x 0.03 and y 0.24 x 0.05 show a broad and frequency-dependent dielectric peak near T m * 766.1 K and 741.7 K, respectively, at zero DC bias E bias. The dielectric peak near T m for these two samples becomes frequency-independent and nearly unchanged, respectively, by applying an E bias = 10 V, which clearly demonstrates a relaxor and dipole glass behavior for the y 0.24 x 0.03 and y 0.24 x 0.05, respectively. In fact, it has been reported that although the relaxor and dipole glass show many similar features in dielectric and FE properties, they differ in essence at least in one aspect, i.e., the relaxor can change into a normal long-range FE/R-FE state under strong external electric fields, while the dipole glass can not [49, 50]. This difference is due to the higher disorder in dipole-dipole interaction and weaker interaction between PNRs or individual electric dipoles in dipole glasses. The e '-T curves for other selected samples are shown in Fig. S4. Similarly, we can also obtain the composition-dependent phase diagram for all the samples by considering all the structural, P -E, and e '-T data discussed above, as summarized in Fig. 1c.
